title: Curve assertions are invariant under forgetting coefficient scalars
statement: Let $k$ be a field, $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ a scheme morphism, and $\Lambda,R$ commutative rings. Let $F$ and $G$ be constructible sheaves of $\Lambda$-modules and $R$-modules respectively on $X_{\mathrm{\acute et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves], [def-constructible-constructible]. Suppose their underlying abelian sheaves are isomorphic. If the eight conditional assertions $\mathcal C(X,G)$ [def-weil-pbc-eight-curve-assertions] hold, then $\mathcal C(X,F)$ holds. No curve, reducedness, finiteness of the coefficient rings, or algebraic closedness assumption is required.

source.place: Theorem 03SC, second proof paragraph (prime-field scalars on the same abelian sheaf)

proof.text: Commutation of the stalk functor with forgetting modules follows from preservation of filtered colimits (Mathlib Point.sheafFiberCompIso). Compose the two commutation isomorphisms and the given abelian isomorphism to obtain a stalk additive equivalence. It preserves nsmul, hence primary and invertible-order torsion.
Apply the functor Sheaf.H to the isomorphism, obtaining inverse equivalences in every degree. Transfer subsingleton and finite groups for C1-C5. Constructibility of both sheaves is assumed.

Naturality of Etale.cohomologyMap with coefficient morphisms conjugates each comparison by the equivalences on the source and pullback. Prove injectivity and surjectivity by composing those equivalences, giving C6-C8.

mathlib_searches.query: A sheaf of modules over a finite ring has a finite filtration whose factors are sheaves of vector spaces over prime fields
Constructible sheaves over finite rings reduce to prime field sheaves by primary decomposition and exact sequence devissage
